input.dimension: argparse help-action short-circuit: which argv tokens pre-empt the exit-1 base58 runtime failures (and the exit-2 argparse errors), turning stdout into the 8-line help and the exit code into 0
rules: CONFIRMED and IMPLEMENTABLE. The question is reachable and highly relevant: a Node port must implement the help short-circuit, because it changes stdout from 0 bytes to 142 bytes and the exit code from 1 (or 2) to 0.

RULE 1 (the exact help payload). When help fires, stdout is EXACTLY these 142 bytes and stderr is EXACTLY 0 bytes, exit code 0: "usage: test15_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --a A
  --b B
  --c C
  --d D
" (8 lines, trailing 
 present, verified with od -c and wc -c=142). Every help-firing form produces the byte-identical payload (md5 prefix 981782ac for -h, --help, --h, --he, --hel, -hh, -hz).

RULE 2 (single-pass, strict left-to-right). Emulate argparse as one left-to-right scan over argv. The FIRST of these events that occurs wins and terminates the program; nothing later in argv is examined: (a) a starved-value error, (b) an 'ignored explicit argument' error, (c) the help action. Verified both directions: `-h --a` -> help/exit 0 (help before starved --a wins) while `--a -h` -> exit 2 'argument --a: expected one argument' (starved --a before -h wins); `-h --help=1` -> help/exit 0 while `--help=1 -h` -> exit 2 'ignored explicit argument'.

RULE 3 (`--` terminates option scanning). The first bare `--` token ends option recognition. Any help token at or after it never fires. The program declares no positionals, so `--` and everything after it become 'extras'. Verified: `--a 1 --b 2 --c z --d z -- -h` -> exit 2, stdout 0 bytes, stderr 'unrecognized arguments: -- -h'; `-- -h -h` -> exit 2 'the following arguments are required: --a, --b, --c, --d'; but `-h --` and `... -h --` and `... -h -- -h` -> help/exit 0. Note `--` is NOT stripped: `--a 1 --b 2 --c z --d z --` -> exit 2 'unrecognized arguments: --'.

RULE 4 (help-firing token forms, all before the first `--`). Help fires (142 bytes on stdout, exit 0) for: (a) the exact token `-h`; (b) any `--`-prefixed token with NO `=` that is a non-empty unique abbreviation prefix of `--help`, i.e. exactly one of `--h`, `--he`, `--hel`, `--help`; (c) a single-dash cluster `-h<rest>` where rest is non-empty AND rest[0] != '-' AND the token contains no `=` immediately after `-h`. Verified firing: -hh, -hhh, -hx, -hz, -ha, -hA, -h0, -h9, -h_, -h., -h/, -h+, -h,, -h:, -h!, '-h ' (all rc=0, 142 bytes).

RULE 5 (near-miss tokens that do NOT fire help). All of these leave stdout at 0 bytes and exit 2. (a) Explicit-argument forms -> exit 2 'argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '<val>'': `-h=1`, `-h=` (val ''), `--h=1`, `--help=1`, `--help=` (val ''), and also `-h-` (val '-'), `-h--` (val '--'), `-h-h` (val '-h'). (b) Tokens that are simply not the help option and fall into extras: `-H`, `-xh`, `-1h`, `--HELP`, `--helpx`, `--help-`, `--help.`, `--h-`, `--hex`, `--hp`, `--elp`, `---h`, `-1`, `-` -> exit 2 with 'the following arguments are required: ...' if any of --a/--b/--c/--d is missing, else 'unrecognized arguments: <tok>'. Help matching is case-sensitive and exact-prefix only.

RULE 6 (value positions never trigger help). When a space-separated token follows --a/--b/--c/--d, argparse refuses to consume an option-looking token as that option's value: `--a --help ...`, `--a 1 --b -h ...`, `--a 1 --b 2 --c -h ...`, `--a 1 --b 2 --c z --d -h`, and `--a --` all -> exit 2 'argument --X: expected one argument', stdout 0 bytes. Per RULE 2 this starvation error also pre-empts any LATER -h in argv (`--a --b 2 --c z --d z -h` -> exit 2, not help).

RULE 7 (`=` form takes the value literally, no help). `--a=-h` -> exit 0 with stdout "b'4TR'
b's'
b'9'
b'9'
"; `--a=--help` -> exit 0 first line b'PVpxBGNs'; `--a=--` -> exit 0 first line b'4SQ'. And `--c=-h` / `--d=--help` -> exit 1 (base58 decode of the literal string fails), stdout 0 bytes. So `=`-attached help-looking values are ordinary strings.

RULE 8 (help beats 'unrecognized arguments' regardless of order). Unknown options are only collected and reported AFTER parsing completes, so they never pre-empt help: `--zzz -h` -> help/exit 0 AND `-h --zzz` -> help/exit 0; `--a 1 --b 2 --c z --d z --zzz -h` -> help/exit 0.

RULE 9 (help beats every runtime failure). All four base58 operations run only after parsing succeeds, so help pre-empts them: `--a 1 --b 2 --c '!!!' --d z` -> exit 1, stdout 0 bytes (ValueError: Invalid character '!'), but with a trailing `-h` -> help/exit 0. `--a $'\xff' --b 2 --c z --d z` -> exit 1, stdout 0 bytes (UnicodeEncodeError surrogates not allowed), with `-h` -> help/exit 0. Even all-four-invalid `--a $'\xed\xa0\x80' --b $'\xff' --c 0OIl --d '!!!'` -> exit 1 / 0 bytes, and +`-h` -> help/exit 0.

RULE 10 (exit-1 stdout is always exactly 0 bytes; no partial output). All four encode/decode calls run before the first print, so any single failure yields 0 bytes on stdout. Verified for a failure in each of the four slots (--a bad, --b bad, --c bad, --d bad) -> rc=1, out_b=0 in every case. A port must therefore buffer all four results and print only on total success.

RULE 11 (help exit code is 0 and there is no stderr). For -h/--help/--h/--he/--hel/-hh/-hz: rc=0, stderr byte count 0, stdout 142 bytes. Argparse errors (exit 2) write usage+error to stderr and 0 bytes to stdout. Runtime failures (exit 1) write a traceback plus a PyInstaller line to stderr and 0 bytes to stdout.

RULE 12 (help text width depends on COLUMNS - pin it to 80). The 142-byte payload is what you get when COLUMNS is unset (the case in this environment; stdout is a pipe so Python falls back to width 80). COLUMNS=80 is byte-identical to the default (cmp passes). COLUMNS=20 re-wraps to 174 bytes across 14 lines. COLUMNS=200 and COLUMNS= (empty) and COLUMNS=abc all give the same 142 bytes. LC_ALL=C and PYTHONIOENCODING=latin-1 do not change the bytes. A Node port should hardcode the 80-column rendering.

RULE 13 (prog name comes from argv[0] basename). Running the same binary copied to /tmp/zz_renamed yields 'usage: zz_renamed [-h] ...' (135 bytes). If the harness always invokes it as test15_executable, hardcode 'test15_executable'; otherwise derive from basename(argv[0]). The same prog name appears in the exit-2 usage/error lines on stderr.

RULE 14 (things a naive port gets wrong - test these). A port that (a) runs base58 before/independently of the help action, (b) only recognizes the literal strings '-h' and '--help', (c) treats `--a -h` as a help request, (d) treats `-h` after `--` as help, (e) accepts `-h=1` as help, or (f) prints partial lines before a decode error, will diverge on stdout and/or exit code on the cases enumerated above.
